newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians say four Arabs die because of curfew.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians say four Arabs die because of curfew.

text.p: A Palestinian health official charged on Monday that four Arabs died in a West Bank village under Israeli army curfew because they were not allowed to travel to hospital.

An Israeli military spokesman, commenting on reports that three Palestinians died in the village of Sourif, denied they were prevented from going to hospital and said he was checking on the allegations of a fourth death.

Doctor Musa Abu Hmied, general-director of Palestinian hospitals in the West Bank, said a resident physician in Sourif confirmed Palestinian newspaper reports that two adults and a newborn baby died in the past three days because of lack of access to outside medical treatment.
Hmied told Reuters a fourth Palestinian from Sourif, 61-year-old Khaled Ayesh, died at a military checkpoint when his family tried to send him to hospital after he suffered chest pains.

Sourif's 13,000 Palestinians have been under curfew since Thursday when the Israeli army found in the village the body of a soldier it said had been kidnapped and killed in September by militants from the militant Moslem group Hamas.

The military spokesman said he had no information about Ayesh but "checks by the army and Israeli Civil Adminstration showed there was no connection between the curfew and the deaths of three villagers, who died of natural causes".
He said Israeli security forces were under orders to allow "urgent medical cases" to leave areas under curfew.

Palestinians charged last March that at least two Arabs -- an elderly woman from Gaza and an infant boy from the West Bank -- died because Israeli soldiers imposing travel bans delayed vehicles taking patients to hospitals.
The Israeli army said in June it would pay $7,800 in compensation to the infant's family.
Palestinians have reported at least one case in which an Arab women delivered twins at an Israeli army checkpoint while waiting for permission to travel to hospital and both babies died.
